title: KĀLA-YANTRA v3 launch configuration, the input of fleet/kyqualify.py (relaunch plan v2.7 §7 launch line and launch qualification KV-06, §14 B-0c)
description: One role's launch line as data: everything a qualification receipt binds. kyqualify.py builds the argv from it as: claude_bin -p --setting-sources project --permission-mode <permission_mode> --model <model> --effort <effort> --max-turns <max_turns> <extra_flags…> --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <mcp_config> [--disallowedTools <disallowed_tools…>] --output-format stream-json --verbose [--add-dir <dir> per add_dirs]. prompt_path is the role prompt or card whose hash is bound; it is not sent during qualification. Shape only. Not checked by this schema, and checked by kyqualify.py before anything is launched: paths normalised; worktree, claude_bin (executable), mcp_config and prompt_path present on disk, and the worktree's .claude/settings.json — when there is one — a readable regular file (its sha256, or "absent", is bound and a byte copy of it is in force in every canary project); the program version (2.1.296 or newer); a value policy for every env_names entry (HOME/USER from the caller, LANG, TERM, PATH = child_path and ZDOTDIR fixed, TMPDIR and JOB_SCRATCH that qualification run's own directories, KY_* conventional or from the caller — KY_SCRATCH is the campaign scratch root — anything else refused) and the six plan §7 basics present; no tool both intended and denied, no intended tool in disallowed_tools, bash_canary only when Bash is intended or denied, denied_bash only when Bash is intended. A missing or non-positive max_turns or deadline_seconds refuses for every role (plan §7).

engine.description: Absent (as in every Claude Code configuration written before the second engine) or "claude". An OpenAI Codex CLI configuration says "codex" and is described by launch_config_codex.json instead.

_note.description: Free text for people; never read by the harness and never bound.

bash_canary.description: Which Bash canary to use (default 'write'). 'write': `printf %s <nonce> > <file>`, the file must exist afterwards. 'readonly': `shasum -a 256 <file>` on a file the harness wrote; the reply must contain the SHA-256 the harness computed itself and no file may change on disk - for roles whose shell is restricted to read-only commands.

shell_canary.description: How the harness words the shell commands of its long-running canary (the timeout and termination probes need a live tool child) and of its PATH canary (default 'plain'). 'plain': `sleep 600` and `printf 'KYQ-PATH=%s\n' "$PATH"`. 'python3': the same through `python3 -c …`, for a role whose shell allows python3 and little else.

denied_bash.description: Shell commands that must be refused with no effect although Bash itself is an intended tool. Each runs once, in a canary project that is also a scratch `git init` repository, so a file, index, HEAD, ref or configuration change is observable; pass = nothing changed AND a permission denial of exactly that command was observed. Plain words, relative names and options only (a command runs inside the scratch repository if its denial fails): no path separator, no '~', no '..', no shell syntax.

role.description: Names the receipt run/QUALIFICATIONS/<role>-<model>.json and the one-shot launchd label in.marsys.kalayantra.qualify.<role>.

deadline_seconds.description: The role's wall-clock deadline; bound, and the upper limit of every canary run.

env_names.description: The job's whole environment, by name (env -i semantics); values follow kyqualify.py's value policy. Every job carries JOB_SCRATCH and KY_SCRATCH (rework ruling R1).

child_path.description: The PATH value: absolute entries separated by ':'; an empty entry would be the current directory.

extra_flags.description: The EXTRA_LEAN_FLAGS chosen by the B-0c probes: flags only, each '--name' or '--name=value' (a bare word would become the prompt). Never a flag that changes where settings, permissions, sign-in or MCP servers come from, and never one the launch line sets itself.

disallowed_tools.description: Tool names (removed from the offered tools) and permission rules of the form Bash(<glob>) (the tool stays offered; a matching call is denied — deny rules beat allow rules, the project's included). Passed as separate arguments after --disallowedTools.

intended_tools.description: Tools the role must be able to use without a TTY or a permission prompt; one observable canary each.

denied_tools.description: Tools the role must NOT be able to use: the same canary must leave no effect and a denial must be observed.
